lines.text: You uprooted a vine from Egypt;
You drove out the nations and transplanted it.
You cleared the ground for it,
and it took root and filled the land.
The mountains were covered by its shade,
and the mighty cedars with its branches.
It sent out its branches to the Sea,
and its shoots toward the River.
Why have You broken down its walls,
so that all who pass by pick its fruit?
The boar from the forest ravages it,
and the creatures of the field feed upon it.
Return, O God of Hosts, we pray!
Look down from heaven and see!
Attend to this vine—
the root Your right hand has planted,
the son You have raised up for Yourself.
Your vine has been cut down and burned;
they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.
Let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand,
on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself.
Then we will not turn away from You;
revive us, and we will call on Your name.
Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts;
cause Your face to shine upon us,
that we may be saved.

pictures.scene: Hermann David Salomon Corrodi, On the Banks of the Nile — the river of Egypt with its palms standing along the bank, You uprooted a vine from Egypt, You drove out the nations and transplanted it

pictures.scene: Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka, Magányos cédrus — the one great cedar holding out its branches over the hills, the mountains were covered by its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches
pictures.name: pd_csontvary_maganyos_cedrus

pictures.scene: Salomon van Ruysdael, Zeilschepen op breed binnenwater — the sails carried out across the wide water toward the river mouth, it sent out its branches to the Sea, and its shoots toward the River
pictures.name: pd_ruysdael_zeilschepen_binnenwater

pictures.scene: Carl Gustav Carus, Gotisches Fenster in der Ruine des Klosters Oybin — the broken wall and the empty window standing open to anyone who passes, why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit
pictures.name: pd_carus_gotisches_fenster_oybin

pictures.scene: Frans Snyders, The Boar Hunt — the boar out of the forest turned on the dogs and trampling the ground, the boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed upon it
pictures.name: pd_snyders_boar_hunt

pictures.scene: Jan Matejko, Kazanie Skargi — the preacher standing up before the whole court with both hands lifted to heaven, return O God of Hosts we pray, look down from heaven and see
pictures.name: pd_matejko_kazanie_skargi

pictures.scene: Silvestro Lega, Il pergolato — the vine trained over the trellis where the household sits in its shade, attend to this vine, the root Your right hand has planted
pictures.name: pd_lega_il_pergolato

pictures.scene: Ferdinand Hodler, Der Holzfäller — the axe swung back at full stretch against the standing trunk, the son You have raised up for Yourself, Your vine has been cut down and burned
pictures.name: pd_hodler_holzfaeller

pictures.scene: Cornelis Claesz van Wieringen, The Spanish Armada off the English Coast — the great fleet caught out at sea with men and horses thrown into the water, they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance, let Your hand be upon the man at Your right hand
pictures.name: pd_wieringen_spaanse_armada

pictures.scene: John Everett Millais, Christ in the House of His Parents — the boy standing between His mother and the carpenter's reaching hands, on the son of man You have raised up for Yourself, then we will not turn away from You
pictures.name: pd_millais_house_of_his_parents

pictures.scene: George Inness, The Rainbow in the Berkshire Hills — the bow standing over the green hills once the storm has gone by, revive us and we will call on Your name, restore us O LORD God of Hosts
pictures.name: pd_inness_rainbow_berkshire

pictures.scene: Alfred Thompson Bricher, A Quiet Day near Manchester — the whole bay lying open and full of light, cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved
pictures.name: pd_bricher_quiet_day_manchester
